title: Two critical RCEs in PHP core
description: Two critical unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, affect PHP core versions since 5.4. These flaws, collectively dubbed “php2shell,” can be triggered by a plain HTTP request before any application code runs. The vulnerabilities arise from improper handling of out-of-memory conditions and use-after-free stale internal states. The impact spans the entire PHP ecosystem, including popular applications like WordPress, Drupal, Magento, and others. PHP 8.1 and older versions are end-of-life and will not receive patches, while PHP 8.2 support ends December 31, 2026. No active exploitation has been observed as of October 21, 2026. Cisco Talos recommends immediate upgrading to fixed releases and provides intrusion prevention signatures for detection. Some configuration mitigations may reduce exposure but do not fully protect against these vulnerabilities.
aiSummary: Cisco Talos disclosed two critical RCE vulnerabilities in PHP core, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both scoring 9.2 on CVSS v4.0. CVE-2026-109618 occurs due to out-of-memory handling interrupting PHP during partial request data initialization, causing request cleanup to treat invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 involves reuse of stale internal state after its backing memory has been freed before normal initialization. These vulnerabilities affect every PHP build since version 5.4 and can be exploited via a plain HTTP request before application code execution. The vulnerabilities impact a broad range of PHP-based applications and hosting environments. PHP 8.1 and older are unsupported and unpatched; PHP 8.2 support ends late 2026. Cisco Talos provides SNORT signatures for detection and recommends upgrading to fixed PHP releases. Mitigations include configuration changes such as setting memory_limit to -1 and adjusting upload limits for CVE-2026-109618, and disabling session.upload_progress and adjusting fatal_error_backtraces for CVE-2026-109619, though these do not fully mitigate the risk.
aiImpact: The vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP core, potentially enabling attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems. The impact is widespread across the PHP ecosystem, affecting numerous popular applications and hosting platforms. Systems running unsupported PHP versions (8.1 and older) will not receive patches, increasing risk. Exploitation could be leveraged by state-sponsored, ransomware, and financially motivated threat actors. No active exploitation has been observed yet, but the potential blast radius is large due to PHP's extensive use.
